palette.reason: Coherent families (orange brick, cream trim, blue glass, green crowns) with no clipping or black holes (0 % clipped), and the crowns now sit near the pack's summer green (about #64753E); but the sky is pale periwinkle (about #9FB3D6, S 0.25) against the anchor's and mock's clear blue (S 0.50), the lawn is minty (about #99B57B, hue 90) where the mock is olive (hue 74), the asphalt is lifted and blue (about #8C95A2 lit against #777B7F), the walk is near white (#EAE2DF) and the drive band is a saturated slate blue (#5A7391).

light.reason: One coherent sun from the left: crown tops are lit and tree shadows fall right and toward the camera across lawn and road, as bearing 45 requires; but the day is hazy and low-contrast, the left block's east and north faces are the same value (about #9E653A) so the masses are flat-lit, the foreground trunk is flat (lit and shaded halves within 7 %, where the mock's differ by about 30 %) and the pale sky gives no clear-afternoon depth.

softnessAO.reason: Cast shadows on road and lawn are soft-edged, crown undersides darken gently and nothing floats or has black seams; but the foreground trunk is a bare cylinder with no flare or contact darkening, and the plinth, stoop cheeks and window reveals carry no eave or contact shadow.

groundRichness.reason: Seams and edge clusters carry it: sidewalk joints, a slab walk, a white curb line, grass tufts on the far parkway and a three-lobe shrub bed; but both lawns are one flat mint tone (only a soft 10 % gradient and tree shadows), with no worn edges, leaf litter or patchiness, so this is a weak 3.

depthFog.reason: Far crowns and houses lighten and soften slightly toward a pale vanishing point and the sky pales at the horizon, giving usable separation with no fog seam; but near, mid and far crowns stay about equally saturated and the street end has little haze, so the tonal steps are weak.

houseVariety.reason: Several kit families: a long 3-storey court-style block, two-storey flat-roof brick two-flats with stoops and cornices, a cream-faced house and a pitched-roof house far off; but everything is one orange-brick tone with plain stoops, and no bays, porches, railings or garages show.

geography.reason: Heading 270 with the sun at azimuth 225 ahead-left and out of frame: tree and trunk shadows fall right and toward the camera, matching bearing 45, and the lit sides of trunks face left; the block is on the south (left) side and the houses on the north (right) side of a straight west-running street, and nothing contradicts the camera or sun. No map overlay, so not 5.

adGroundRich.reason: A three-lobe foundation bed at the block's far corner, a continuous hedge and egg-shaped shrubs at the far stoops, and grass tufts on the parkway earn the 3; the lawns are one flat tone with hard edges, and there are no mulch beds, leaf litter or worn edges, and the near plinth has no planting.

adRegional.reason: A brick court block and two-flats with stoops, cream trim, flat parapets and teal doors on a tree-lined parkway street read as Lakeview, but the brick is more orange (S 0.63) than the mock's muted red-brown (S 0.45), the trees are one family, and no alley, garage, gangway, bay or rear-porch cue shows, so it stays somewhat generic.

topFixes.fix: Retune the surface tones to the mock and the fall anchor: warm olive lawns (about #8A9562, hue 74) in place of the mint, a darker neutral asphalt (about #777B7F lit, #5A6573 in crown shade) in place of the pale blue-grey, a warm beige walk (about #D2C9BC) in place of the near-white, recolour the saturated slate-blue drive band as grey concrete or asphalt, and add 10 to 20 percent contact darkening at the foreground trunk base, the plinth and the stoop.
topFixes.why: Lit asphalt measures about #8C95A2 against the mock's #777B7F and the anchor's #616175, the lawn about #99B57B (hue 90) against #8A9562 (hue 74), the walk #EAE2DF against #D2C9BC, and the drive band is a saturated slate blue (#5A7391, S 0.38) where the mock's is grey (S 0.14); the trunk meets the lawn with no darkening.

topFixes.fix: Deepen the sky to the pack's clear gradient (zenith about #73A5CC, mid #A2C4DC, pale warm-white horizon #DBDCD1), pull the violet cast back toward cerulean (hue 218 toward 209) and add two or three simple white cumulus with cool grey undersides, so a clear 41 degree afternoon reads as clear.
topFixes.why: The visible sky measures about #9FB3D6 (S 0.25, hue 218) against the mock's about #72ADE7 (S 0.50, hue 209) and the anchor's #7AB3F8; the pale lilac sky makes the afternoon read hazy and soft.

topFixes.fix: Give the brick masses relief that reads at phone size: replace the flat tan base with a brick base under a cream stone string course, add sills and a cornice cap, mute the brick to a red-brown (S about 0.45) with a darker shaded long facade, and vary the right-hand houses with hipped grey roofs, a bay front, a gabled porch house, buff or cream brick and black iron stoop railings.
topFixes.why: The big left wall is a flat orange slab (about #9E653A, S 0.63) above a flat tan base with no coursing, belt course or cornice, and the right-hand houses are mostly flat-roof boxes with plain stoops; the mock and the Chicago block show brick coursing, cream stone bands, grey hipped roofs, bays, gables, porches and railings.

grade.vsPrevious: better: saturation now matches the mock (dSat +3.0 against +13.3), the asphalt is darker (lit about #8C95A2 against #B0B0B5) and the crown greens are lighter and nearer the mock's (about #64753E against #415604), but the left lawn lost its olive-yellow patch and is now a uniform mint, and the sky, flat facades and flat trunk are unchanged.
grade.summary: At phone size the street reads as a coherent Lakeview brick block with parkway trees and a sensible sun, nearer the mock than the last run in road, crown and saturation, but hazy and pale: a periwinkle sky, mint lawns, a lifted blue-grey road and a saturated blue drive band. The biggest gap to the mock is that sky-and-surface tone (cerulean sky, olive lawns, dark neutral asphalt), followed by flat, unrelieved brick facades.

LF-ground.reason: groundRichness 3 and adGroundRich 3; layers visible are the lawn, cream walk, slab walk, drive band, parkway grass with tufts and a foundation shrub bed with hedges; grass stays off the road and the block is dense; a marginal pass because the lawns are flat and there are no mulch beds or litter.

LF-light.reason: light 3 and palette 3; shadows fall right and toward the camera as bearing 45 requires, summer reads as summer, trunks stay distinct from crowns and lawn and exposure is unclipped (p5 88, p95 227); facade modelling is weak (the left block's two faces are the same value) but windows, trim and stoops still read.

LF-trees.reason: silhouettes 3, adRegional 3 and the season is right, but the crown left of the foreground trunk is stacked spheres on a bare pole, the small mid-right tree is a three-ball lollipop and the far left row repeats one round crown (section V faults); outranked by the three larger fixes above: merge crowns into unequal lobes around forked branches and vary by family (open elm or honey locust against closed maple).

LF-sky.reason: no astronomy error (the sun is out of frame, no disk) and the cloud stays simple, but the sky is pale periwinkle (about #9FB3D6, S 0.25) with a lilac cast and does not strengthen palette, light or depth for a clear 41 degree afternoon; covered by top fix 2.

gaps: Sky and surface tone: the sky is pale periwinkle (about #9FB3D6, S 0.25) where the mock is cerulean (about #72ADE7, S 0.50) with crisp white cumulus; the lawn is minty (about #99B57B, hue 90) against olive (about #8A9562, hue 74); the asphalt is lifted and blue (about #8C95A2 lit) against neutral grey (about #777B7F); the drive band is a saturated slate blue (#5A7391) where the mock's is grey (#88919E); the walk is near white (#EAE2DF) against warm beige (#D2C9BC), so the frame reads hazy where the mock reads clear.

Facades: a flat saturated orange slab (about #9E653A, S 0.63 against the mock's muted red-brown S 0.45) over a flat tan base, with no brick coursing, cream string course or cornice, and the right-hand houses are mostly flat boxes where the mock has grey hipped roofs and bay fronts.

Trunk and contact: the foreground trunk is a flat grey-brown cylinder (lit and shaded halves within 7 %) where the mock's is a warm brown with a clearly lit side (about 30 % lit-to-shade), with no contact darkening at its base.

Forms: nearly every house is a flat-roof brick box with a plain stoop (plus the one 3-storey slab) and only one distant pitched roof shows, where the block mixes gabled cottage fronts with porches, bay-front two-flats, hipped grey roofs and cornices of different profiles.

Materials and palette: one orange brick family with cream trim and teal doors, flat colour with no coursing over a flat tan base; the block mixes red, buff, cream and grey masonry with dark roofs, white trim and black iron railings.

Yards: plain flat lawns with one small shrub cluster and a far-side hedge, and no porches, garages or railings read; the block has trimmed foundation hedges and rounded or conical shrubs on every frontage, mulched beds and railed front steps.
